pr_title: filetable: allow overwrite during BACKUP and fix delete bug
pr_body:
BACKUP should be able to overwrite files written to userfile.
Previously, we had an existence check preventing files with the
same name from being written again, now we Delete the old file
before attempting to write the new one (in the same txn).
This only applies to BACKUP, userfile upload still prevents dup
files from being uploaded.

This change also fixes a bug which was introduced to deletion
when we switched over to using UUIDs.

Lastly, this change removes the txn retry loop from userfile storage
and moves it to where the chunk is being written to the tables. This
was needed because txn retries were missing reading bytes between retry
runs because of the manner in which they are sent from the copy machine.

Addded BACKUP/RESTORE unit tests for userfile.

Fixes: #53995

Release justification: bug fixes and low-risk updates to new functionality
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/53926)
This is RFAL. It includes the changes to the WriteFile txn semantics discussed on Slack.
stressrace is passing locally for both the unit tests locally, but its failing with a timeout when run on CI. Trying to see if it is the MultiNode one or the SingleNode one.

issue_context.title: userfile storage rejects attempts to overwrite files
issue_context.body: BACKUP requires the ability to overwrite files in the ExternalStorage it is writing to, egs: BACKUP-CHECKPOINT is written at multiple stages throughout a BACKUP. Userfile rejects any attempts to write files with the same name twice, thereby not working well with BACKUP semantics.

review_comments:
The reason I marked this as a WIP is that I need some help understanding why the new userfile Backup and Restore test behaves the way it does.
- Testing locally, I am able to BACKUP/RESTORE tables and databases correctly (no error thrown).
- The commented out implementation of this test also does not raise any errors.

When I switch to using some of the more involved infrastructure we have for testing the BACKUP/RESTORE of database data, I get a  `pq: importing span /Table/53/1{-/100}: checksum mismatch for 586866600006090753.sst` when the `RESTORE` stmt is runs. All the BACKUP verification steps before it run fine. I'm wondering whether it is something to do with how userfile chunks its data, I'm not sure how to debug this further?

@dt @miretskiy

I also realized that if I set the splits to 0 when generating the bank data in `backupRestoreTestSetupWithParams` and remove the index created on data.bank, the restore goes through fine. I'm not sure how all these things tie together to cause that checksum mismatch.

I looked into this a bit and I think it looks like it has to do with the userfile being able to handle retries (within `WriteFile`). I think the fix would look something like https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/53940.

Thanks for looking into this Paul, I'm wondering if it is better to just eliminate the possibility of a txn retry in WriteFile and switch to using the internal executor to just `BEGIN, COMMIT/ROLLBACK`.

This also simplifies the interaction with the copy machine which wraps an `io.PipeReader` in a `noopSeeker` currently. Implementing seek on a pipe reader where we don't have access to all the data at once seems complicated? We would need some buffering/state logic. @miretskiy do you have any inputs here?

~Hmm, I think that the retry semantics are useful since the transaction may get a retry request. But it looks like only the creation of writer needs to be transactional, so it looks like we can move the writing of the data outside the txn?~
Edit: Ah, I see the payload writer is passed the txn to use.
